title: The Branch from Jesse
summary: A prophecy foretells a rod from Jesse’s stem, a branch from his roots, and the Spirit of the Lord resting upon him.

explicit_facts.text: A rod shall come forth from the stem of Jesse, and a branch shall grow from his roots.
The Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, with wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear of the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A plant motif may symbolize the prophecy without presenting its fulfillment as a witnessed event.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of “him” are not specified.
No setting or visible appearance of the Spirit is specified.

narration.text: And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots.
And the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses present a prophecy, not a present witnessed event.
The rod and branch are prophetic imagery, not grounds for inventing a literal supernatural scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Jesse or the figure referred to as “him” as physically present.
Do not invent the figure’s identity or appearance, or give the Spirit an unmentioned visible form.

title: Righteous Judgment
summary: The prophecy describes a figure who will understand in the fear of the Lord, judge the poor with righteousness, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.

explicit_facts.text: He shall be made quick of understanding in the fear of the Lord and shall not judge by sight or reprove by hearing.
He shall judge the poor with righteousness and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.
The prophecy says he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth and slay the wicked with the breath of his lips.
Righteousness and faithfulness are described as girdles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A text-focused presentation can convey the prophecy without showing its figures of speech as physical acts.
unspecified_visual_details: The figure’s appearance and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: But with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The rod of his mouth and breath of his lips are prophetic figures of speech, not a narrated combat scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal violence or invent the figure’s identity or appearance.

title: Creatures at Peace
summary: The prophecy pictures animals dwelling and feeding together, with a little child leading them.

explicit_facts.text: A wolf dwells with a lamb; a leopard lies with a kid; a calf, young lion, and fatling are together; a little child leads them.
A cow and bear feed, their young lie down together, and a lion eats straw like an ox.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The animals may be depicted peacefully together as described.
unspecified_visual_details: The animals’ and child’s appearances, and the landscape, are unspecified.

narration.text: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb
and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic imagery, not a present witnessed event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add animals, people, or a named location.

title: No Harm in the Holy Mountain
summary: The prophecy describes children near serpents without harm and declares that nothing will hurt or destroy in the holy mountain.

explicit_facts.text: A suckling child plays on the hole of the asp, and a weaned child puts a hand on the cockatrice’s den.
Nothing shall hurt or destroy in the holy mountain, and the earth shall be full of knowledge of the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The children and serpents may be shown in a peaceful setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The children’s and serpents’ appearances and the mountain terrain are unspecified.

narration.text: They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain
for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic imagery, not a present witnessed event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show injury or add details of danger beyond the stated imagery.

title: An Ensign for the People
summary: The root of Jesse stands as an ensign sought by the Gentiles; his rest is glorious.

explicit_facts.text: The root of Jesse stands as an ensign for the people; the Gentiles seek to it, and his rest is glorious.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The ensign may be represented symbolically without specifying its design.
unspecified_visual_details: The figure’s appearance, the ensign’s design, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: there shall be a root of Jesse
which shall stand for an ensign of the people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic language, not a present witnessed gathering.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the figure’s appearance or the ensign’s markings.

title: The Remnant Gathered
summary: The prophecy says the Lord will recover the remnant of his people from the named regions, set up an ensign for the nations, assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather the dispersed of Judah.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord will act a second time to recover the remnant of his people from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.
He will set up an ensign for the nations, assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic depiction could suggest a gathering without specifying a route, time, or assembly place.
unspecified_visual_details: The people's appearance, the ensign's design, and the Lord's appearance and manner of acting are not described.

narration.text: And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic future events, not a present-tense narrated gathering.
The Lord setting his hand and the four corners of the earth need not be depicted literally.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the Lord's visible appearance, the ensign's design, a specific gathering site, or a present-tense gathering.

title: Ephraim and Judah
summary: The prophecy says Ephraim’s envy will depart and that Ephraim and Judah will no longer vex or envy one another.

explicit_facts.text: Ephraim’s envy departs, Judah’s adversaries are cut off, Ephraim does not envy Judah, and Judah does not vex Ephraim.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching may be represented symbolically, without staging a specific encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether Ephraim and Judah are represented as individuals or groups, and their appearance and setting, are unspecified.

narration.text: and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic language, not a narrated present conflict or reconciliation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a battle or identify specific people as Ephraim or Judah.

title: The Nations and the Remnant
summary: The prophecy says an unidentified group will fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the west, spoil those of the east together, lay their hand upon Edom and Moab, and receive the obedience of the children of Ammon.

explicit_facts.text: An unidentified group shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines towards the west and spoil those of the east together.
They shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon shall obey them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophecy can be represented symbolically rather than as a specific battle.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of “they” are unspecified.
No specific setting or combat encounter is described.

narration.text: they shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon shall obey them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a prophecy, not a narrated present-tense event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify “they” or invent a specific battle.

title: The Way Through the Waters
summary: The prophecy says the Lord will destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea, strike the river into seven streams so men can cross dry-shod, and provide a highway for the remnant left from Assyria.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord shall destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea and, with his mighty wind, shake his hand over the river and smite it in seven streams, making men go over dry-shod.
There shall be a highway for the remnant of his people left from Assyria, compared with Israel coming up out of Egypt.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A prophetic visualization may show men crossing dry ground where the river has been divided into seven streams.
unspecified_visual_details: The river’s identity, the highway’s form, the people’s appearance, and the Lord’s appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: And the Lord shall utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his mighty wind he shall shake his hand over the river, and shall smite it in the seven streams, and make men go over dry shod.
And there shall be a highway for the remnant of his people which shall be left, from Assyria,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is the first-person narrator, but these verses contain no first-person speech.
These are future prophetic statements, not a present crossing. Israel’s departure from Egypt is a comparison, not a simultaneous event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Israel’s departure from Egypt as occurring in this scene.
Do not identify the river or invent the Lord’s appearance.
Do not present the foretold events as already occurring.
